Operation and Maintenance Manual
Two-axis slant-bed CNC lathe with 12-station turret and MC-8T control
Document numberMTC420-OM-EN
Revision
Valid for C (2025-03)
MTC-420 from serial number MTC420-23-0100
Language English (translation of the original instructions)
Demo document. Morvane Werkzeugmaschinen and the MTC-420 are fictional and were created for the HealthyFac demo data.

Contents
1 About This Manual 2 Safety 3 Transport and Installation 4 Commissioning 5 Machine Description 6 Technical Data 7 Operation 8 Monitored Signals and Operating Limits 9 Alarms and Messages 10 Maintenance 11 Troubleshooting 12 Electrical Data 13 Spare Parts 14 Decommissioning and Disposal

1 About This Manual
This manual describes the transport, installation, commissioning, operation, monitoring, maintenance, and decommissioning of the MTC-420 CNC turning center. It is the translation of the original instructions in German. If the two texts differ, the German text applies.
The manual is written for three target groups. Operators load workpieces, start programs, and do the daily checks. Maintenance technicians do the periodic maintenance and simple repairs; they need a mechanical or electrical qualification. Morvane service does the tasks that are marked as such, for example the spindle bearing replacement and the geometry check.
Keep this manual at the machine for its full service life. Give it to the next owner if you sell the machine.

Symbols and Signal Words
DANGER, Meaning = A hazard that causes death or severe injury if you do not avoid it.. WARNING, Meaning = A hazard that can cause death or severe injury.. CAUTION, Meaning = A hazard that can cause a minor injury.. NOTICE, Meaning = A risk of damage to the machine or the workpiece.

Related Documents
Programming manual MC-8T, Number = MC8T-PRG-EN. Programming manual MC-8T, Content = G codes, cycles, tool data, program management. Alarm manual MC-8T, Number = MC8T-ALM-EN. Alarm manual MC-8T, Content = Control alarms 10000 to 39999 (NC kernel, drives, PLC system). Circuit diagram, Number = MTC420-EP-24-0187. Circuit diagram, Content = Wiring of this machine (in the electrical cabinet). Hydraulic diagram, Number = MTC420-HY-C. Hydraulic diagram, Content = Hydraulic unit, chuck and tailstock circuits. Chip conveyor manual, Number = CC2-OM-EN. Chip conveyor manual, Content = Hinged belt conveyor CC-2

Revision History
A, Date = 2023-02. A, Change = First edition.. B, Date = 2023-10. B, Change = New vibration limits after field tests; alarm A111 added.. C, Date = 2025-03. C, Change = Coolant concentration target changed to 6 to 8 %; maintenance interval of the hydraulic oil changed to 2,000 h.

Intended Use
The MTC-420 is intended for the turning, drilling, and threading of metal workpieces (steel, cast iron, aluminium, brass) in industrial use. The workpiece must fit within the working range of chapter 6 and must be clamped in the chuck, and supported by the tailstock when it is longer than 3 times its diameter.
Any other use is not intended. Foreseeable misuse includes: machining magnesium without a fire protection system, machining wood or plastics that produce fine dust, running with the guard door bridged, and using chucks that are not approved for the spindle speed.
DANGER - Rotating chuck. Never open the guard door or reach into the work area while the spindle turns. The door interlock stops the spindle, but a spindle that coasts down can still cause severe injury.
WARNING - Hydraulic clamping. The chuck clamps the workpiece with hydraulic pressure. If the hydraulic pressure falls below 25 bar, the clamping force is no longer guaranteed and the workpiece can be thrown out of the chuck.
WARNING - Chuck speed limit. Each chuck has a maximum speed that is engraved on it. The control limits the spindle speed to the value in the chuck data (parameter P2210). Enter the correct value after each chuck change.

Residual Risks
Workpiece or jaw thrown out, Where = Work area. Workpiece or jaw thrown out, Protective measure = Guard door with polycarbonate window, rated for the maximum chuck energy; hydraulic pressure monitoring (A201).. Cuts from chips and tools, Where = Work area, chip conveyor. Cuts from chips and tools, Protective measure = Chip hook, gloves only when the spindle is off.. Skin irritation from coolant, Where = Work area, coolant tank. Skin irritation from coolant, Protective measure = Correct concentration, skin protection plan, regular coolant change.. Electric shock, Where = Electrical cabinet. Electric shock, Protective measure = Cabinet lock, work only by qualified electricians with the main switch locked out. The DC link of the drives holds a voltage for 5 minutes after switch-off.. Hot surfaces, Where = Spindle housing, hydraulic unit. Hot surfaces, Protective measure = Temperature up to 60 °C during operation. Let the parts cool down before maintenance.. Noise, Where = Operator position. Noise, Protective measure = Emission sound pressure level 78 dB(A). Wear hearing protection for long shifts near open machines.

Safety Devices and Test Intervals
Emergency stop buttons (2), Function = Stop all motion (stop category 1). Emergency stop buttons (2), Test = Press each button during a slow spindle run. Emergency stop buttons (2), Interval = Weekly
Guard door interlock, Function = Locks the door while the spindle turns; stops the spindle when opened in manual mode. Guard door interlock, Test = Try to open the door at 50 rpm; the door must stay locked. Guard door interlock, Interval = Weekly. Enabling switch (handwheel), Function = Allows motion in manual mode with the door open. Enabling switch (handwheel), Test = Release the switch during an axis motion. Enabling switch (handwheel), Interval = Monthly. Hydraulic pressure switch, Function = Prevents the spindle start below 25 bar. Hydraulic pressure switch, Test = Lower the pressure at the reducing valve during maintenance. Hydraulic pressure switch, Interval = Every 2,000 h. Polycarbonate window, Function = Retains parts. Polycarbonate window, Test = Visual check for cracks, cloudiness, coolant damage. Replace after 5 years or after a hit.. Polycarbonate window, Interval = Weekly / 5 years

Lockout Procedure
1. Stop the program and set the mode to off.
2. Switch off the main switch Q1 and lock it with your personal padlock.
3. Wait 5 minutes. Check with a voltmeter that the DC link of the drives is below 50 V.
4. Release the hydraulic pressure: open the chuck once with the foot pedal, then switch off the hydraulic unit.
5. Put a tag with your name and the date on the main switch.

Transport
The machine is delivered on a wooden skid with the X and Z axes locked by red transport brackets. Lift the machine only at the four lifting eyes with a lifting beam and four slings of at least 2 m length. Do not lift it at the turret or the spindle housing. The center of gravity is marked on the machine with a yellow label.
Transport weight (with skid), Value = 4,650 kg. Transport dimensions (L x W x H), Value = 3,150 x 1,900 x 2,050 mm. Lifting points, Value = 4 lifting eyes M30, on the machine base. Storage temperature, Value = -10 to 50 °C, dry, protected from frost if coolant was filled

Foundation and Space
The machine needs a flat industrial concrete floor of at least 200 mm thickness without joints under the machine. The floor load is 2,100 kg/m² over the footprint. Keep a free space of 800 mm at the back for the electrical cabinet door and of 1,000 mm at the chip conveyor outlet.

Levelling
1. Remove the transport brackets of the X and Z axes (keep them for a later transport).
2. Place the 6 levelling pads under the levelling screws.
3. Put a precision level (0.02 mm/m) on the bed guideways, first along Z, then across.
4. Adjust the levelling screws until both directions are within 0.02 mm/m.
5. Tighten the lock nuts and check the level again after 1 week of operation.

Connections
Electrical supply, Requirement = 400 V ±10 %, 3 phases + PE, 50 Hz, fuse 35 A gL, cable 5 x 10 mm². Earth leakage protection type B, 300 mA, if required by local rules.. Compressed air, Requirement = 6 bar, dry and oil-free, connection G 1/2. Used for the chuck air blow and the window cleaning.. Network (option MC8T-IOT), Requirement = Ethernet RJ45 at the cabinet roof; OPC UA port 4840, MQTT client to a plant broker.. Coolant, Requirement = Fill 180 L of water-mixed coolant at 6 to 8 % concentration before the first start.. Hydraulic oil, Requirement = Delivered filled (12 L). Check the level at the sight glass before the first start.

4 Commissioning
Morvane service or a person trained by Morvane does the first commissioning. Record the results in the commissioning report that is delivered with the machine.

Checklist Before the First Start
Transport brackets removed, Expected result = All 4 red brackets removed and stored. Machine level, Expected result = Within 0.02 mm/m in both directions. Phase sequence, Expected result = Correct (the hydraulic pump turns in the arrow direction). Hydraulic oil level, Expected result = Between min and max at the sight glass. Central lubrication, Expected result = Grease reservoir full; 3 manual cycles run without alarm A401. Coolant, Expected result = Tank filled, concentration 6 to 8 %. Emergency stop and door interlock, Expected result = Tested as in chapter 2. Chuck data, Expected result = Maximum chuck speed entered in parameter P2210

First Start
1. Switch on the main switch Q1. The control starts in about 60 seconds.
2. Acknowledge the power-on message and start the hydraulic unit. The pressure must reach 35 bar within 10 seconds.
3. Reference the axes: mode manual, key REF, first X, then Z.
4. Run the warm-up program O9000 (10 minutes).
5. Machine the test workpiece of drawing MTC-TW-01 and measure it. Roundness must be within 0.003 mm and cylindricity within 0.008 mm over 150 mm.
6. Write the spindle temperature, the spindle vibration, and the hydraulic pressure after the warm-up into the commissioning report. These are the reference values for later comparisons.
Reference values of this unit (commissioning 2024-09-16): spindle temperature 36 °C after O9000, spindle vibration 1.1 mm/s at 3,000 rpm, hydraulic pressure 35.5 bar, coolant concentration 7 %.

5 Machine Description
The MTC-420 is a two-axis CNC turning center with a 45-degree slant bed of cast iron. The slant bed lets the chips fall into the chip conveyor and gives the operator good access to the chuck.
Machine bed, Description = Cast iron EN-GJL-300, ribbed, with roller linear guides size 35 for the X and Z axes.. Main spindle, Description = Spindle nose A2-6, bore 66 mm, front and rear angular contact bearings with grease lubrication for life (re-greasing only during a bearing overhaul). Temperature sensor PT100 and vibration sensor at the front bearing.. Spindle drive, Description = AC spindle motor 15 kW, poly-V belt 8PK1200, ratio 1:1.2.. Feed axes, Description = Servo motors with absolute encoders, ball screws 32 x 10 mm, X stroke 230 mm, Z stroke 620 mm.. Turret, Description = Servo turret with 12 stations, VDI 30, Hirth coupling with hydraulic clamping, bidirectional indexing.. Tailstock, Description = Hydraulic quill, MT4, quill stroke 100 mm, thrust 3 to 12 kN, positioned by the Z slide.. Hydraulic unit, Description = Gear pump 8 L/min, 12 L tank, pressure 35 bar, return filter 10 µm, pressure transmitter.. Central lubrication, Description = Piston pump with 2 L grease reservoir, interval 30 min, pressure switch.. Coolant system, Description = 180 L tank, immersion pump 2 bar / 40 L/min, level sensor, temperature sensor, filter basket.. Chip conveyor, Description = Hinged belt conveyor CC-2, outlet height 1,050 mm, runs with the coolant pump or on demand.. Electrical cabinet, Description = Cooling by a filter fan (cabinet temperature monitored), main switch Q1, drives, PLC, power supply 24 V DC.. Control, Description = Morvane MC-8T with 15-inch touch panel, handwheel, signal export option MC8T- IOT.

Unit Identification
The rating plate is on the left side of the electrical cabinet. This copy of the manual was delivered with the unit below.
Model, Value = MTC-420. Serial number, Value = MTC420-24-0187. Year of manufacture, Value = 2024. Control, Value = Morvane MC-8T, software version 4.2. Commissioning date, Value = 2024-09-16. Options, Value = MC8T-IOT (signal export), chip conveyor CC-2

Working Range and Axes
Swing over bed, Value = 560 mm. Maximum turning diameter, Value = 420 mm. Maximum turning length, Value = 600 mm. Bar capacity, Value = 52 mm. Stroke X / Z, Value = 230 / 620 mm. Rapid traverse X / Z, Value = 24 / 30 m/min. Feed force X / Z, Value = 6 / 8 kN. Positioning accuracy (ISO 230-2), Value = 0.005 mm. Repeatability, Value = 0.002 mm

Spindle and Turret
Spindle speed range, Value = 30 to 4,500 rpm. Spindle motor power, Value = 15 kW (30 min), 11 kW (continuous). Spindle torque, Value = 286 Nm (30 min). Chuck size, Value = 8 inch (210 mm), hydraulic three-jaw. Turret stations, Value = 12, VDI 30. Indexing time, adjacent station, Value = 0.2 s

Supply and Environment
Supply voltage, Value = 400 V, 3 phases, 50 Hz, 35 A fuse. Connected load, Value = 28 kVA. Hydraulic system pressure, Value = 35 bar nominal. Coolant tank, Value = 180 L. Compressed air, Value = 6 bar, 150 L/min. Machine weight, Value = 4,300 kg. Footprint (L x W), Value = 2,950 x 1,750 mm. Permitted ambient temperature, Value = 10 to 35 °C. Relative humidity, Value = up to 75 %, no condensation. Emission sound pressure level, Value = 78 dB(A)

Operator Panel
Cycle Start, Function = Starts or continues the active program.. Feed Hold, Function = Stops the axis feed; the spindle keeps turning (message S003).. Mode switch, Function = Selects auto, manual, or off (see 7.2).. Spindle override, Function = 50 to 120 % of the programmed speed.. Feed override, Function = 0 to 150 % of the programmed feed.. Door key, Function = Unlocks the guard door when the spindle is stopped.. Coolant key, Function = Switches the coolant pump on and off in manual mode.. Emergency stop, Function = Stops all motion; release by turning the button.

Operating Modes
The mode switch sets the spindle mode. The control reports the active mode as the signal spindle.mode.
auto, Meaning = The control runs the active program. The guard door must be closed and locked.. manual, Meaning = Set-up mode. The operator moves the axes with the handwheel. With the door open, the spindle speed is limited to 50 rpm and the axis speed to 2 m/min.. off, Meaning = The spindle drive is disabled. The control, the coolant pump, and the hydraulic unit can stay on.

Start of a Shift
1. Check the coolant level and the hydraulic oil level (sight glasses).
2. Switch on the machine and start the hydraulic unit.
3. Reference the axes if the control asks for it (after a power failure).
4. Run the warm-up program O9000. It runs the spindle for 10 minutes in steps from 500 to 3,500 rpm.
5. Check the spindle temperature on the diagnosis screen. After the warm-up, 30 to 45 °C is typical.
NOTICE. A cold spindle that runs at full speed at once wears its bearings faster and can show a short temperature alarm.

End of a Shift
1. Finish the program and move the turret to the home position.
2. Remove chips from the work area and the turret with a brush.
3. Close the coolant nozzles' valves so that the coolant does not drain into the work area.
4. Set the mode to off. Leave the main switch on if the machine is used in the next shift.

8 Monitored Signals and Operating Limits
The table lists every signal that the MC-8T control reports. The normal range is the range for continuous operation. A value in the warning range is allowed for a short time but needs attention. A value at the alarm limit stops the machine.

8 Monitored Signals and Operating Limits
Spindle temperature. The sensor sits at the front spindle bearing. A rise of more than 5 °C within 15 minutes at a constant speed is an early sign of a bearing or lubrication problem, also when the value is still in the normal range. Compare the value after the warm-up with the reference value of the commissioning report.
Vibration. The vibration limits follow ISO 10816-3 for machines of group 2 on a rigid foundation. Measure on the spindle housing in the radial direction. A new machine shows 0.8 to 1.5 mm/s. An unbalanced chuck

documentChunks.text:
Signal Export (Option MC8T-IOT)
The control publishes the signals every 5 seconds to an MQTT broker or offers them as OPC UA variables. The MQTT payload is a JSON object with the sample time and one property per signal key. Status codes are sent as a list of active codes. Example:
```
{ "sampledAt": "2025-04-02T08:15:05Z", "metrics": { "spindle.temperature": 41.2, "spindle.speed": 2800, "spindle.load": 64, "spindle.vibration": 1.3, "door.open": false, "spindle.mode": "auto", "coolant.level": 71 }, "statuses": ["S002"] }
```

9 Alarms and Messages
The control shows each alarm with its code on the screen and stores it in the alarm history (last 1,000 entries). An error stops the program and the spindle. A warning lets the current program finish. An info message needs no action. Control alarms with five digits (for example 21612) are described in the alarm manual MC8T-ALM-EN.

Spindle (100)
A101, Type = Error. A101, Text = Spindle overtemperature. A101, Cause and action = The spindle bearing temperature is above 70 °C. Let the spindle cool down to below 45 °C. Check the belt tension and the spindle cooling fins. If the alarm comes back within 1 week, have the spindle bearings inspected by Morvane service.. A102, Type = Error. A102, Text = Spindle overload. A102, Cause and action = The spindle load was above 120 % for more than 10 s. Reduce the depth of cut or the feed rate. Check the insert for wear; a blunt insert raises the load by 20 to 40 %.. A103, Type = Error. A103, Text = Spindle speed deviation. A103, Cause and action = The actual speed differs by more than 10 % from the set speed for 2 s. Check the belt for slip and the spindle encoder cable.. A104, Type = Error. A104, Text = Spindle drive fault. A104, Cause and action = The spindle drive reported a fault. Read the drive code on the diagnosis screen (alarm manual MC8T-ALM-EN).. A110, Type = Warning. A110, Text = Spindle vibration high. A110, Cause and action = The vibration is above 4.5 mm/s. Check the balance of the chuck and the workpiece and the clamping of long workpieces. Plan a vibration analysis if the value stays high.. A111, Type = Error. A111, Text = Spindle vibration too high. A111, Cause and action = The vibration is above 7.1 mm/s. The spindle stops. Do not restart before the cause is found: loose chuck, damaged bearing, loose belt pulley.. A112, Type = Warning. A112, Text = Spindle temperature rising fast. A112, Cause and action = The temperature rose by more than 5 °C within 15 minutes at a constant speed. Reduce the speed and watch the trend. Check the lubrication state of the bearings at the next stop.

Hydraulics (200)
A201, Type = Error. A201, Text = Hydraulic pressure low. A201, Cause and action = The hydraulic pressure is below 25 bar. The chuck clamping is not safe; the spindle cannot start. Check the oil level, the pressure setting (35 bar), and the hoses for leaks.. A202, Type = Warning. A202, Text = Hydraulic return filter clogged. A202, Cause and action = The filter indicator switched. Replace the return filter element MV-420-2210 within 1 week.. A203, Type = Warning. A203, Text = Hydraulic oil temperature high. A203, Cause and action = The oil temperature is above 55 °C. Check the oil level and the cooler fins of the hydraulic unit. A hot ambient raises the oil temperature.
A204, Type = Error. A204, Text = Hydraulic oil overtemperature. A204, Cause and action = The oil temperature is above 65 °C. The hydraulic unit stops; the chuck stays clamped by the check valve. Let the oil cool down and find the cause before the restart.. A205, Type = Warning. A205, Text = Hydraulic oil level low. A205, Cause and action = The level switch reports a low level. Add oil ISO VG 32 and look for leaks.

Coolant and chips (300)
A301, Type = Error. A301, Text = Coolant pump motor overload. A301, Cause and action = The motor protection of the coolant pump tripped. Check the pump for chips and the filter basket.. A302, Type = Error. A302, Text = Chip conveyor overload. A302, Cause and action = The conveyor stopped because of a jam. Run the conveyor backwards for 5 s, remove the jam, and restart.. A305, Type = Warning. A305, Text = Coolant level low. A305, Cause and action = The coolant level is below 25 %. Add coolant at a concentration of 6 to 8 % before the end of the shift.. A306, Type = Error. A306, Text = Coolant level critical. A306, Cause and action = The coolant level is below 10 %. The coolant pump stops to protect itself from dry running. Fill the tank and acknowledge the alarm.. A307, Type = Warning. A307, Text = Coolant temperature high. A307, Cause and action = The coolant is above 35 °C. Thermal growth of the workpiece can affect the size. Check the tank level; consider a coolant chiller in summer.

Lubrication (400)
A401, Type = Error. A401, Text = Lubrication fault. A401, Cause and action = The central lubrication pump built no pressure in 3 cycles in a row. Check the grease reservoir and the pump. Do not run the axes without lubrication for more than 1 hour.. A402, Type = Warning. A402, Text = Grease reservoir low. A402, Cause and action = The grease reservoir is below 20 %. Refill grease NLGI class 00.

Safety (500)
A501, Type = Error. A501, Text = Door open in automatic mode. A501, Cause and action = The guard door was opened while a program ran in auto mode. Close the door and restart the program from the last block.. A502, Type = Error. A502, Text = Door lock fault. A502, Cause and action = The door lock did not reach its position. Check the lock and the door alignment.. A503, Type = Error. A503, Text = Emergency stop active. A503, Cause and action = An emergency stop button is pressed. Release it and acknowledge.. A504, Type = Error. A504, Text = Chuck not clamped. A504, Cause and action = The clamp sensor reports no clamped state at the program start. Check the jaw stroke and the sensor position.

Axes and turret (600 and 700)
A601, Type = Error. A601, Text = X axis following error. A601, Cause and action = The X axis deviates more than allowed from its path. Check for a collision and for chips on the guide covers.. A602, Type = Error. A602, Text = Z axis following error. A602, Cause and action = As A601 for the Z axis.. A603, Type = Error. A603, Text = Software limit switch. A603, Cause and action = The program moves an axis outside its stroke. Correct the program or the work offset.. A604, Type = Warning. A604, Text = Axis reference lost. A604, Cause and action = The absolute position was lost (encoder battery). Replace the encoder battery and reference the axis.. A701, Type = Error. A701, Text = Turret not clamped. A701, Cause and action = The turret did not reach its clamped position after indexing. Check the hydraulic pressure and the turret for chips.. A702, Type = Error. A702, Text = Turret indexing timeout. A702, Cause and action = The indexing took longer than 2 s. Check the turret motor and the clamping.

Electrical cabinet (800)
A801, Type = Warning. A801, Text = Cabinet temperature high. A801, Cause and action = The cabinet temperature is above 45 °C. Clean or replace the filter mat. Check the cabinet fan.. A802, Type = Error. A802, Text = Cabinet overtemperature. A802, Cause and action = The cabinet temperature is above 50 °C. The drives stop to protect the electronics. Find the cause before the restart.. A803, Type = Warning. A803, Text = 24 V supply low. A803, Cause and action = The 24 V DC supply is below 22 V. Check the power supply and the load.

Maintenance and states (900 and S)
M900, Type = Warning. M900, Text = Maintenance due. M900, Cause and action = The operating hours reached the next maintenance interval of chapter 10. Do the listed tasks and reset the counter on the maintenance screen.. M901, Type = Info. M901, Text = Encoder battery due. M901, Cause and action = Replace the encoder batteries within 4 weeks (every 2 years).. S001, Type = Info. S001, Text = Ready. S001, Cause and action = The machine is ready for a program start.. S002, Type = Info. S002, Text = Cycle running. S002, Cause and action = A program runs in auto mode.. S003, Type = Info. S003, Text = Feed hold. S003, Cause and action = The operator stopped the axis feed. Press Cycle Start to continue.. S004, Type = Info. S004, Text = Warm-up running. S004, Cause and action = The warm-up program O9000 runs.

10 Maintenance
The intervals count operating hours (signal machine.operating_hours) or calendar time, whichever comes first. The control shows message M900 when a 500-hour interval is reached. Record each task in the maintenance log (section 10.4). Lock out the machine (chapter 2) before every task inside the work area or the cabinet.

Maintenance Schedule
Each shift, Task = Check the coolant level and the hydraulic oil level. Remove chips from the work area and the turret. Run the warm-up program O9000.. Each shift, Time = 10 min. Each shift, Who = Operator. Weekly, Task = Measure the coolant concentration with a refractometer (target 6 to 8 %). Clean the chip conveyor filter basket. Check the guard door window for cracks. Check the grease level of the central lubrication. Test the emergency stop buttons and the door interlock.. Weekly, Time = 30 min. Weekly, Who = Operator. 500 h or 3 months, Task = Clean the coolant tank and change the coolant. Check the poly- V belt tension. Clean the electrical cabinet filter mat. Check the chuck jaws for wear and grease the chuck. Check the wipers of the guide covers.. 500 h or 3 months, Time = 2 h. 500 h or 3 months, Who = Maintenance technician. 2,000 h or 1 year, Task = Change the hydraulic oil (12 L, ISO VG 32) and the return filter. Check the backlash of the X and Z axes (limit 0.008 mm). Check the turret clamping and the coolant nozzles. Replace the cabinet filter mat. Test the hydraulic pressure switch.. 2,000 h or 1 year, Time = 4 h. 2,000 h or 1 year, Who = Maintenance technician. 2 years, Task = Replace the encoder batteries of the X and Z axes (with the control switched on).. 2 years, Time = 20 min. 2 years, Who = Maintenance technician. 8,000 h or 4 years, Task = Inspect the spindle bearings (vibration analysis and run-out check, limit 0.003 mm). Replace the poly-V belt. Check the ball screws and the linear guides. Check the geometry with a test workpiece.. 8,000 h or 4 years, Time = 1 day. 8,000 h or 4 years, Who = Morvane service. 5 years, Task = Replace the polycarbonate window of the guard door.. 5 years, Time = 1 h. 5 years, Who = Maintenance technician

Check the Poly-V Belt Tension
1. Lock out the machine and remove the rear cover of the spindle drive.
2. Press the belt in the middle between the pulleys with a spring scale at 50 N.
3. The deflection must be 4 to 5 mm. Adjust the motor plate with the two tension screws if needed.
4. A belt with cracks, shiny flanks, or missing ribs must be replaced (MV-420-1150).
documentChunks.location: page 17: Check the Poly-V Belt Tension

documentChunks.text:
Change the Hydraulic Oil
1. Run the machine for 15 minutes so that the oil is warm and the dirt is in suspension.
2. Lock out the machine. Place a 15 L container under the drain valve of the hydraulic tank.

5 Installation
5. Foundation. Place the base plate on a concrete foundation with a mass of at least 1.5 times the mass of the pump set. Level the base plate to 0.2 mm/m and grout it after the alignment.
6. Suction pipe. Install a straight suction pipe with a length of at least 5 times its diameter before the suction flange. The pipe must rise continuously to the pump (no air pockets). Use an eccentric reducer with the flat side on top.
7. Discharge pipe. Install a check valve and a shut-off valve after the pump. Install a minimum flow bypass if the plant can close all consumers.
8. Pipe forces. Support the pipes so that they put no load on the pump flanges. Check: the flange bolts must slide into the holes without force.
9. Alignment. Align the motor to the pump with a dial gauge or a laser tool. Allowed misalignment: 0.05 mm radial and 0.05 mm per 100 mm axial. Check the alignment again after the pipes are connected and after the first 24 hours of operation.
10. Instruments. Fit pressure transmitters on the suction and on the discharge side, a flow meter in the discharge pipe, and temperature and vibration sensors on both bearing housings. Connect the leakage sensor in the seal chamber port (G 1/4).
11. Electrical connection. A qualified electrician connects the motor as shown in the terminal box (star-delta or converter). Set the motor protection to the rated current of 33.5 A.
